text: Service and food are on standards here at this McDonald's but there is nothing special about this one. The last time I was hear they messed up everything. Don't go here.

$.69 for any size coffee you say?  Breakfast sandwiches comprised of egg, meat and cheese crammed between two syrupy pancakes?  Granted eating here 3 times a day will take 10 years off your life, but once in a while never hurt anyone.

This Mickey-Dee's is located across the street from the Silver Legacy Hotel/Casino. Matt took advantage of the free coffee promotion from 5am-7am. So have a lot of the sad looking people patronizing there, who appeared to lost big, all their hard-earned money on gambling.

Matt ordered a Egg McMuffin and Hot-cakes along with the FREE COFFEE to go, because this McDonald's is kind of a "Nasty". It is also kinda pathetic to go to any fast-food restaurant on your lengthy vacation, but anything that is free, why not?

Ever since *that* movie, I've been apprehensive of the golden arches. Burger King? Sure. Taco bell? No problem. But those golden arches. No thanks.

I just haven't been back. Until today. 

Today I arrived at the McDonalds on Upper State, expecting to be greeted by the familiar, horrible, green and yellow decor. I wasn't disapointed, (although this was the last time today) as the green and yellow trash bins were the first thing I saw as I exited my car. But something was wrong. These trash bins were shoved into a forlorn corner of the parking lot.

Throwing open the entry door, I stepped inside, sidestepped an orange traffic cone and a dropcloth, and walked into a mod, airy, antiseptic airport lounge. The old reliable green and yellow had been replaced with an adult lounge of earth tones, brushed aluminum and pub-style tables. 

But I couldn't dwell on the interior too long, as I had to look out for the painter who was painting the ceiling and shuffling around those dust-laden ceiling tiles. 

I stepped up to the counter to place my order - 10 chicken nuggets, please. At least the food is still inexpensive. 

I was left to wait next to my friend the painter until my food was up. Once my number was called I eagerly snatched the bag and high-tailed it out of there.

At home, I opened up my nice 40% post-consumer recycled fiber paper bag to find 10 consistent, piping hot little nuggets of processed chicken and two containers of barbecue sauce, as requested. 9 chicken nuggets later (1 chicken nugget was set aside for my sugar-momma of the evening) I was left with a passable level of satisfaction. 

The interior was cold and impersonal and the service was institutional. The nuggets tasted fine, if not memorable, which is fine by me, as I'd rather forget the whole experience anyway.

4 stars for being there for me after midnight on my way back to the hotel with a board advertising 99 cent chocolate dipped cones ... I honestly can't remember the last time I had one ... and boy did it not disappoint considering I had the "ate dinner too early" munchies. Minus 1 star for the isolated cashier behind what I hope was bullet proof glass and the metal extend-a-drawer like they have at some bank drive-thrus ... made me question the safety of my temporary digs.

Memorable rating: 4 out of 5 (the grilled chicken salads are worth coming back for)

Battle of the Fast Food salads:
Southwest Salad
Asian Salad
Both with grilled chicken are definitely a twist over BK's Tendergrill and much lighter than Wendy's salads...

I dont eat too many burgers from fast food joints anymore... and a fast salad is something important to me nowadays...
and McD's  has definitely come through with a nice selection...

Jack in the Crack has some new salads too..
Thats where im heading tomorrow....

enough said...

Don't give money to the homeless so they can buy booze. Buy them a couple burgers and fries at this newly remodeled midtown McDonalds. The Ronald people razed the old one to the ground and put up a more sterile one. So next time you get panhandled for "money for food" in Centennial Park, take time to walk across the street to mickey d's and help those poor souls with food.

No drive-through?  And it's off of a freeway?  You're kidding, right?

Nope.

And my apologies to my fellow Yelpers for my influx of fast food-related reviews lately -- money is tight!

Andy is right. this has to be the worst mcdonalds ever.  i will not deny that i am one of the few people left in the world who actually enjoys mcdonalds, but this particular one is just awful.

from the homeless people pestering you nonstop, to shadiness going on in the bathrooms, combined with the fact that it takes the workers there about 20 minutes to give you your meal, makes this mcdonalds one to avoid.

on my last trip there, i saw a lady changing her infant son's crappy diaper on one of the tables.

Hahahaha... so happy to see these other 2 reviews! This has absolutely got to be the shittiest McDonald's on the planet. The drive-thru people yell at you, then ask you to pull over and wait for your food. After 15 minutes I finally backed into the drive-thru line again and blocked everyone from getting their food until they gave me mine. Everyone was honking and screaming and I thought I was going to get shot... what a rush! As mentioned, it is more of a homeless shelter than anything. "Alright, McGriddle!"

I looked up this McDonald's specifically because most of my other reviews are all positive, so I thought to myself "What is the absolutely worst place in Philly I have been to?" This is my answer.

It's a McDonald's... so you already know what you're in for.

I was excited when I drove by to find out this one had a 24 hour drive-thru, thinking it was the closest to Downtown, but I just learned the one on Lindell near Sarah is *also* 24 hours. Fast-food nation, indeed.

It's worth noting this is the closest McDonald's to SLU and Downtown with a 24 hour drive-thru. Next time you wake up (or are *still* up) at 3 AM and desire that fast-food fix, here ya go.

I have absolutely no idea how that affects their breakfast vs. normal food hours, but I'm interested to find out.

It's pretty bad. Really, what do you expect, greatness? You won't get it, though you will get soggy fries and the typical Big Mac.

From what I hear, they would tear this place down to make room for new development, but McDonald's doesn't allow it. 

Burger King across the street was shown the door, why can't McDonald's get the hint?

This McDonald's is right in Bryn Mawr, off of Airdale Road. Like most of their suburban locations, there's decent parking. However, I've only been here (and twice) for drive thru service - in fact, I made a late night run for Chicken McNuggets, only because it was Sunday night and even WENDY'S was closed. No problems with service here!

The young woman who took our order looked miserable and was not friendly at all.   There were only 2 clean tables in the entire place.   There was an "odd" guy staring and walking around the restaurant.  We questioned the staff about him and was told ....that is Chester and he comes in every day to buy a coffee and walks around.    He made me very uncomfortable as I tried to enjoy my cheeseburger, fries, and chicken tenders.

you would think that visiting mc donalds during the lunch rush would mean fresh fries and double cheese burgers that have either spent enough time under the warmer to slightly melt the cheese or (if you're lucky) have been made with freshly grilled meat to melt the cheese.

today (at a relatively busy 12:30pm), i received neither.  my fries were the "sitting out for a few hours" kind (with no salt?), and the double cheese burger was downright cold. cheese, meat, everything.  really disappointing.

This McDonald's is amazing.  The food and service are strictly typical as far as McDonald's go.  But what they have here that makes them worthy for mention among their peers, is a hilariously disconcerting environment.  

Imagine this with me.  You sidle up to the counter and order yourself a Big Mac combo.  You get your food, the fries look a little worse for wear, and fill up your fountain drink with Coke.  Then you take a seat in a leather, high-backed chair and watch the live music at the baby grand piano up on the stage.  Like so many things in Broadripple Village that could only have been conceived at the juncture of bored and rich, this McDonald's is unorthodox.  For those of you not interested in watching the pianist, they have more than enough copies of old Reader's Digest compilations laying about to read.

If you need to grab a quick and cheap bite in Broadripple, this is just about your only option.  And it does not disappoint by leaving the theme of the district.

Typical McDonald's restaurant... the wait time for the drive-in was ridiculously long (we went at 10pm... that could be why, since nothing else for miles was open).  Still, the apple pie wasn't bad and the BLT ranch sandwich wasn't bad either...  But nothing was standout exceptional.. unfortunately that's what happens when these foods get  eaten over and over and are available anywhere... But when nothing else is open, you can rely on McDonald's :)

It's a McDonalds.

Sorry; they don't have the best fries; they're in fact the worst.

I already go super rarely, if they got rid of double cheeseburgers and McChickens on the dollar menu, I'd stop all together.

Burger King uber alles.

Despite its location in a generally wealthy neighborhood, this McDonald's performs poorly, even in comparison to other McDonald's franchises. The weekday daytime manager, or at least the one I've encountered during the mid-to-late Summer does not have a good handle on things. The service has been severely lacking, and the food and beverage quality has been sub-standard. For example the root beer wasn't made anywhere near right for weeks (I'm not sure of the exact time frame because I've stopped going there. 

Even for McDonald's, this is a sad excuse.

So I wouldn't usually bother to review a McDonald's but this one makes me so mad so often I felt the need to announce it to the world. Open 24 hrs? Ha! They are always closed without explanation (though I see you inside!) from 3-5 a.m. The way my schedule is, this is a regular meal time for me.

How hard is it to say "Open 22 hrs"? I could forgive you then.

If I had to choose a McDonald's (and unless I'm so desperate, let's hope it never comes to this), then this is the one I would go to. This was my McD's growing up and as scary as it may sound, I've seen some of the same people for the last 5-10 years working here. Those are the ones who will give you the best service, it seems. For others, it may just be a temporary thing, so you may not get the best.

A lot of the McD's have gotten upgrades so that they look similar to the one near CAPA. When this location got rid of most of the booths (which were frequently inhabited by the seniors), it began to look a lot more empty because of the extra space. The booths in the center were replaced by higher stools and small tables. At least it didn't look as dingy anymore.

I never liked the new "habitrail" feel of the Play Place that took over about 10 or so years ago. Growing up, we had an AWESOME play place. Grimace, Hamburglar themed attractions.

There is metered street parking on Broad and the surrounding areas. It is conveniently located near a bank, 2 pharmacies, a dollar store, and public transportation. Southern is also nearby so don't be surprised seeing this place crawling with kids.

One star for being the world's largest fast food chain.

One star for the Ronald McDonald House & charities.

One star for their fries & hot apple cinnamon turnover.

Other than that, I would not eat here!  

My husband has a friend in Fall River, Ma. that has a dairy farm. When one of the old cows gives up and falls down or gets sick, it goes to auction, I kid you not!  ( A Dairy Cow).  Burger King buys, or used to, these cows for beef products, I will never, ever eat a fast food burger after knowing that!  

Frozen fried, formed fish sandwich, minus one star.

Chicken sandwich is a turn off when you bite into a piece of gristle, so minus one more star.

Get the fries and the turnover, when in a hurry and hungry or don't.

This is by far the best McDonald's I have ever seen!
I ate here for breakfast, because that's all McDonald's is really good for anyway.  But they have Dinosaurs outside with a Dino learning center inside, with fossils and posters, even dinosaur wall paper.  The learning center isn't very extensive, but it's still very cool.  I wish all McDonald's had learning centers inside, whether it be Dinosaurs, Space Science, Ocean, etc.  Brilliant idea, I think.  You can also take pictures outside with large  dinosaurs! 
Way to go Tucson!

If you have a craving for McDonalds don't expect this location to satisfy your needs.  The last time we went there they were actually OUT of burgers and last night my friend was having a Big Mac attack but they don't serve them on their "late night menu" AND they were OUT of coke.  Unbelievable.  If you must have McDonalds visit the location on Grey's Ferry over by the Pathmark instead.  The drive thru there is open 24-hours.  The Grey's Ferry location is also known locally as the ODB McDonalds as a rap artist known as Old Dirty Bastard was apprehended by the police while dining there.

This McDonald's is a freestanding one on Henderson Road. Depending on the direction you're driving from, it's either convenient or a total pain in the arse to get into.

Parking isn't bad. I sometimes pick up greasy breakfast sandwiches here (in bulk) as I never run into any issues here. Usually it isn't crowded for breakfast, but I heard the lunch rush can impact service.

There's a drive-thru if you're in a hurry, and if not, take advantage of their free wireless access to see how bad your 401K is doing.

Worst McDonalds of all time.

Not spectagious, splendiferous or special in any way.

Breakfast is the staple of McDonalds, the least common denominator, the lay-up. How do you fuck up breakfast? Its actually tougher to do it wrong.

This McDonalds does it wrong every time. Every day of the damn week. Epic Breakfast fail.

I am in super spite mode due to stale McMuffins all of the last 3 times I have gone.

Dear Ray Crock,

Have your dead corpse shoot god an email and demand new management at the del ave McDonalds so I can get some decent breakfast when I am headed to my warehouse once a week.

Dammit. For a #2 breakfast, which now costs $5.34 with an OJ, you would think its a given that I wouldnt break my tooth on the damn english muffin. Nooks and Crannies my arse, more like tungsten-carbide muffin teeth.

Cmon people! I am definitely "hatin' it".

Cmon Yelp, can't I give a bankrupt Ed McMahon style half star to this p.o.s. fast food restaurant? All in favor of instituting the "half star" say "I". 

I.

The only reason I continue going to any McDonald's is for their Chicken Nuggets, Fish Fillet, and Oreo McFurry's. I go to this location because its the closest one to me. 

This place is pretty big. It has an attached gas station and a mini mart and plenty of seating space. 

Now the staff at this McDonald's is something to talk about. They are so ghetto. You hear them screaming at each other while they try to take and complete your order. You hear curse words left and right. Usually the one in charge is the most ignorant. There are some good people here and they are usually the ones getting reamed for nothing at all. I witnessed a "supervisor" ripping an employee a new one in front of all the customers because he left his lunch on the counter while he went to grab something real quick. I'm glad to hear she is no longer working there although there were a couple more of these incidents before she was fired. I think if they fire a couple more of these people, this place will actually be pretty great.

It's pretty bad even for a McDonald's, guys. For about three months after they opened, it was awesome--the staff was well-trained and polite! But now it's the usual tough-talking teenagers whose priorities are, in this order, 1) talking to coworkers, 2) talking on their phones... 96) running a cash register. Getting your food takes forever no matter what time of day or night. And the extremely loud TVs blaring CNN make me want to kill.

IN SUMMARY
Food freshness: cold by the time you get it
Order accuracy: average
Overall staff attitude: laughably bad
Cleanliness of dining area: very good
Cleanliness of bathrooms: ?
Refills on drinks: yes
Condiments, napkins, utensils: out in the open
Kid's play area: no, although there are some perplexing McDonalds-themed souvenirs in plexiglass cases which they could look at 
Drive-through: yes

Very conveniently located right above the Broad Street line. The employees really make it. Their turnover seems much lower than average and the older women who work here are competent and friendly--no dead-eyed monotones. The *worst* part of this McDonalds is the other customers. It's within one block of a high school, a drug rehab, and a senior home, so it gets the worst of all worlds in terms of your fellow diners. In the morning the joint is full of  old folks gossiping at 70dB and at night it's crammed with cackling adolescents trying to look cool by bragging about their delinquency. Still, if you want fast food served to you by people who treat you like a human being, it's one of your best options.

IN SUMMARY
Food freshness: average to good. Food sometimes sits in the warmer too long. 
Order accuracy: excellent
Overall staff attitude: excellent
Cleanliness of dining area: above average
Cleanliness of bathrooms: average for fast food
Refills on drinks: no
Condiments, napkins, utensils: behind the counter, even napkins and straws
Kid's play area: yes, but it is almost never open
Drive-through: no

This McDonald's doesn't really take your order it decides what you will have for breakfast.  I ordered 2 egg mcmuffin meals with orange juice and the restaurant decided i needed the 2 egg mcmuffin deal a hash brown and an oj which is nice and all if i was eating by myself but when my friend put his hand in the bag, his OJ and hash brown were missin,

I loathe McDonald's and fast food in general, but I did go here once out of sheer desparation, hunger and broke-ass-ed-ness.  I got a $1.00 McChicken Sandwich, no pickles - It came to $1.07 and I just barely had the change scraped together.

What a humbling experience.

I pray it won't happen again.

ZERO Stars for what we referred to as McDEATH when i was a grad student at Penn.  There have been shootings, stabbiong, roberroes and muggings here over the many years.

Yet somehow - McDeath remains open.

Let's not even talk about the "hood" demographic servers and patrons alike.

And of course the scads of loiterers and homeless, down & out West Philly types.

AVOID.  AVOID.

This McDonald's sucks; the staff is rude, the food cold.  Food is left out of orders and you find out when you get home. Do not come here drive up to the McDonald's on Mae Anne...Beware of the Bums too.
It's McDonald's. Sometimes the food is good and the rest of the time you're not high. What else do you need to know?

There comes a time when you need your daily allowance of saturated fats in one sitting. What better place to accomplish said goal than at wholesome Mickey D's? 

Ever since the notorious movie Super-size Me, portions have become, lets just say, less generous. To compensate for the meager servings, I now have to eat 1 Big Mac, 1 Fish, french fries, 1 wrap, and a soda. I will pay in spades in a few years.

Wow, first time I walked in here and was hit by a disgusting smell.... I still cringe today every time I walk in. Apparently it's whatever their cleaner is, mixed with the smell of a college student's vomit on the floor (which happens all too often, if the rolling of the staff's eyes is to be taken into account). I really do feel sorry for them to have to clean up after the mess students make, the local residents are much better about policing their trash.

Speed is efficient and one of the first McDonald's I had seen with the LCD menus back in 2002-ish?

There's a drive-thru? :P

But the Burger King that was removed in favor of the restaurant/Bridge combination across the street was sad, and this is the only thing left really from my initial view of this intersection in 1998... aside from the old Public Library.

As for safety, it's considerably improved from 10 years ago, I would say. There are fewer bums and fewer shady characters as that's been pushed away and further out by the gentrification of the area. Most of the worry now comes from the north, near Market & 40th.

Reviewing McDonald's? You gotta be kidding!? Right? Well, it has the standard food you would expect, good or bad it's the same. What makes this location is the giant tyranusaurus rex they have along the street. There is a dinosaur theme that is carried throughout the place, so when the kids are bored and hungry consider the entertainment value of the Dinosaur McDonald's a Tucson institution.

When I was living in Santa Barbara, they introduced McDonald's cafe drinks (the iced latte = yummy!) that were much better than the ones they then brought to the Bay Area. I often found great coupons in the newspaper for cheap drinks and egg mcmuffin sandwiches. I loved the deals and would sometimes grab an egg mcmuffin on the way to work. I don't think I ever went for lunch or dinner but breakfast and coffee was great!

Not sure why I'm writing a review for McDonalds.   It's McDonalds.  It's exactly as you would expect it to be.

Food is the same.  Manager is nice.  Coffee is better than starbucks.

A McDonald's seems so out of place here amogst the shi-shi shops on Walnut Street.  That and it is a haven for local down & outs seeking a $1 McChicken and a coke or coffee.

I rarely ever set foot in here. (But admittedly I have once or twice.)

Yick!

I've never demanded my money back from any fast food joint...until tonight.

Oh yes, Girly Girl and I decided to stop at the drive-thru at this McDonald's after making a stop at the nearby Target.  First thing out of her mouth was, "What if it's creepy?" after I suggested we eat inside.  I told her it wouldn't be, but decided to just go ahead and take it home rather than eat there.  

So we order some food...it came to about fifteen bucks, though the drive-thru cashier insisted it was actually five dollars and change even after I told her twice that it wasn't.  When it finally did sink in, she again quoted the wrong total and laughed herself silly after realizing what a complete moron she actually was.  Ah well, time to wait for the food.

I noticed the car in front of me had actually turned its engine off while waiting.  I've done the same thing before, but little did I know how long we'd be waiting when it was finally our turn.  Once we got up to the window, the guy who looked like the manager handed me a diet Coke, which the stupid moron running the drive-thru was told to correct when she read off my order.  After this, we had to listen to Mr. Manager complain to his workers, as well as discuss someone being on her period that week.  Great.

After about 15 or 20 minutes of this horseshit and being told our food was going to be "right up," I screamed "ALL RIGHT, ALREADY" at the two dunces behind the window that was cracked open just a bit.  Manager finally shut up long enough to open the window and I started demanding my money back.  He tried the song and dance that they only had ONE FREAKIN' COOK in the back that night, but I insisted.  His bitchy coworker tried to change my mind as well, but I said "Look, this is FAST FOOD, not 'wait twenty minutes food'!"  So they finally handed me my money back and we drove off.

What I don't get is why Mr. Manager person just didn't shut his mouth that was running 100 mph and get the hell back in the kitchen and help out.  But noooooooo, he'd rather be spreading trashy gossip and not caring.  Not even after he looked out the window at one point and saw cars wrapping around the building.  

Suffice it to say this is the shittiest McDonald's I've ever visited.  If you really need some of this crapola, then please, please, please find another one in the area.  This locale deserves no one's business at all.

This location gets most of its points because of the building. It was completely rebuilt and is very nice. The problems are typically the loud staff, sometimes slow service, and fountain drinks that have less than optimal fizz. The food is usually consistent, so it's not a complete loss.

McDonald's!

What?!?!  You can't go wrong with McDonald's.  That is, if you like McD's.  

The food there is good as usual.  Service was quick and friendly.

This one was a little different though.  I've never been to a McDonald's  where there was a large space between the cashiers' station and the kitchen/serving area.  I mean...there was enough room for a 2-way wheelchair "traffic".

Overall, good.

Well today I met a fellow Yelper, and since our meeting was more about meeting then about lunch, and she had her (adorable) 3 year old we opted to go to a McDonald's so the 3 yr old could play! 

We chose this particular McDonald's because it has the glass enclosed play station - you know those slides and nifty tunnels for kids to play in. 

Well we all got food, and it was exactly what you know your gonna get when you go to McDonald's - nothing great, but something to eat! 

I have a couple of complaints about this place that REALLY need some attention. Starting with the minor complaint - the self serve ice machine didn't work so I had to get them to fill the glasses with ice - seems like they would have known this and gave us ice when they gave us the empty glasses? No big deal

My main complaint about this place is the play area was FILTHY. All of the tables were dirty, the floor was dirty, and it had a funny smell in there. We sat there for a couple of hours talking and never did any staff come out to clean off the tables. 

I know that kids are generally resilient creatures, but I think McDonald's should put a little more care into the sanitation of their children's areas or just DONT have them! Right now with the swine flu going around killing people, everyone, and every restaurant no matter if its McDonald's or a gourmet restaurant should be taking EXTRA steps to keep tables sanitized and things clean - this place was just really out of line, it needs a GOOD scrub down and more attention all the way around! I think a picnic or take out and the park is a better choice next time! At least the rain washes off the tables at the park!!

BTW - it was awesome meeting a fellow Yelper in real life, and she is just as cool in person as she is on Yelp!! Ironically she lived right down the street from me! 

1 star for McDonalds 5 stars for the new cool friend!

I had the extreme pleasure of meeting the above Yelper and she is right on the money...EWWWW. It was starting to rain, so the inside Play Place at a McDonalds seemed like the happening place to go so we could talk while my little one played. Besides smelling like urine, not one table was cleaned! No one ever came in! My daughters socks were BLACK when we were done and she only went up and down two or three times. I like totally disinfected her from head to toe when we got home!

The Food at this McDonald's is good.  I always get my food nice and hot.  The only thing that makes this location bad is the fact that the service is horrible.  You place your order and sometimes have to wait 10 minutes just to get your food.  Even when there is no line.

Stopped here with the kids on the way back home from camping at Refugio. Nice little MickeyDs. Sports memorabelia everywhere, friendly staff and nice bathrooms. The kids were so tired they started to fall asleep while they were eating. Food was as expected. That's all I'll say about that.

An usual McDonalds except of couple of things i noticed on their menu. Some of their items are up by at least 20cents and another one is that the water cost 27cents. Good thing is that they are located right next to circus circus.

I have always valued McDonald's as a fast food chain for its convenience and its very reasonable prices compared to its competitors.  However, I have had several negative experiences there recently.  I went into purchase lunch severalmonths ago, purchased my food and walked toward a table at which to sit down.  I was harrassed about the location of my seat by another customer, and when I protested to the customer, I was harrassed by the check-out person behind the counter who yelled across the restaurant that I was, "rude to their customers."  I as politely as possible under my very frazzed and embarrassed circumstances mentioned that, I too, with a lunch in front of me, was a customer as well and that I was not an employee.  I was asked to leave and did so.

On several separate occassions, I have been asked to leave on the basis that customers complained about my presence--which I feel is inappropriate as a paying customer.  This rudeness has extended so far as to have them ask me to take eat-in oders out of the restaurant.

I have also witnessed several occasions on which large groups of people are rudely kicked out of the restaurant well before the restaurant was slated to close (sometimes 15-20 minutes beforehand, in fact) with out any adequate explanation.

This is not the type of customer experience that people expect when they are paying to enjoy a relaxing and family-friendly eating experience.

My love for McDonald's french fries cannot be stifled by knowledge of their shameless corporation. I read Fast Food Nation and I just don't care.

THIS LOCATION HAS THE FRESHEST FRIES IN ALL OF PHILLY. 

I'm telling you. Every. Single. Time. Hot, salty, french fries. Your mouth wants some right now.

And the burgers are always pretty good here, too. I mean, as good as your gonna get from freakin' McDonald's. They taste like they were just made, no matter the time of day. And the staff is always on point and friendly (for this part of the city, you know).

Props, Girard McD's. You keep up the good work and I'll keep getting my late night fries (and hot fudge sundae, for dipping)!
Nice inside. Big indoor PlayPlace with air hockey and basketball.

I NEVER review chains since you always know what you're going to get when you go there.  Also, I hate fast food so it's pointless giving places 1-3 stars. 

However, I was very impressed with this McDonalds, so I feel it deserves a good rating. My friend and I were staying at the Vandy Marriott for the CMA fest, and overslept the 1030 breakfast cutoff. However, we were craving Egg McMuffins. This McDonalds gave us breakfast 30-45 minutes after the cutoff.  I don't know if this is just a 'southern hospitality' thing, but this never happens in the west!

I went through the drive-through late one night a couple months ago and the dollar menu was gone.  I promptly drove away empty handed.

Buh-bye McDonalds.

1) There is no drive through here.
2) The service was slow and bad.
3) It is a pain to get in and out of because of its proximity to the freeway, stop signs, and bad traffic in general.  And it only has the one driveway.

Skip it.  Go further in either direction on the freeway to get to another McDonald's, especially if you're going to a quick bite.  It's not to be had here.

With moderate customer service, and a constant high-pitched beeping in the kitchen, I tend to avoid McDonald's. It seems that every couple orders or so, they give you the wrong thing. Don't get me wrong - if greasy fast food is your thing, you will love their food. But you might not be so satisfied with their customer service.

My star rating is based in the fact it is a fast food restrant and I am judging it against what I expect from a fast food place.

This McDonalds alway has quick and accurate service.  The eating area is normally clean.

So there aren't a lot of fast food places in the Camby area and I don't really crave fast food.  I do however really like McDonald's breakfast especially their coffee.  This place is literally less than 5 minutes fro my apartment.  I come in around 7:30 or 7:45 several mornings a week.  The drive thru is always long and the staff inside of the McDonalds is ALWAYS slow.  The employees are nice but my goodness they take their sweet time.  I am not the most patient person in the morning but it should not take me 10 minutes to order a large coffee.  There are usually no more than 1 or 2 customers in line ahead of me.  So, why is the drive thru line faster than going inside? WHY?!!!  I continue to go and I continue having my patience tested with the slow dining area. 

WHEW....glad to have gotten that off of my chest!!

Ok after serving over 1 billion people when do you think they will understand that hot mean with steam and service with a smile (does help) but if you know what it know you just get coffee and move on.. I had to wait for food every other time and it not hot too.. just close and restaff

Why would anyone write a review of McDonalds?  Simple.  This is the worst McDonald's on the planet.  

I should tell you that I don't eat McDonald's.  I swore it off after reading Fast Food Nation - & didn't eat it much prior.

But my daughter enjoys their salads so once in awhile I'd pick one up at the drive thru for her.  They get the order wrong EVERY SINGLE TIME.  EVERY SINGLE F#$%ING TIME!  How can this be?  Are their staff brain dead?  Order a Chicken Ranch salad?  You'll get an Asian salad w/ Ranch dressing.  Seriously bad.  

Try going inside.  Your shoes will stick to the floor it's so filthy.  Should be condemned by the health department.

So I have decided I must be glutton for McDonald's punishment.  As previously mentioned I am not the biggest fan of Starbuck's coffee but I do enjoy Mickey D's.  What I don't enjoy is how much their service has declined over the years.  I will only spend a second on my soapbox regarding service that you receive in an "urban" neighborhood compared to a suburb.  I think that service is service and it should be good no matter what "hood" you are in.

Okay back to THIS McDonald's.  How many people does it take to take my coffee order???  Try 3!! My goodness I would have hated if I ordered an apple pie or something.  I have seen a more organized place.  You got 3 people running around but they really weren't doing anything.  You probably had 3 people in line waiting to order.  There are side conversations going on..COME ONE!!  Get with the program.  

I will truly never understand...

If it a MCD owned/managed by "Blessed and Faith" McDonalds of Indianapolis, you will get piss poor service and they will screw it up.  They will not accept the coupons that come from corporate, or they will try to get you to buy something else.  Actually b/c of this particular franchisee, I have not made a purchase at MCD for anything in over a year.  And I don't miss it.  And since some of the "higher" end burger joints like Steak N Shake are offering cheap combos nowadayz, I get my unhealthy, quick burger fixes there.
I tried to tell people about their burgers not being hot... but my friend just would learn... again cold hot food... temp temp temp... not hard to do hot should be hot and cold should be cold

This Mc Donalds is to me one of the worse ever ,the customer service is not good at all,The milk shake machine is down almost 3 days of every week ,the employees were cursing and playing while the line was to the door.My order was incomplete no napkins ,straws or even a have a nice day was said to any customer in the lines.It was just poor service all around

Getting off of the shitty New Century bus, starving and grossed out,  we headed over to this McDonald's to use the bathroom and grab a snack. 

This turned out to be the perfect Philly welcome. 

I was able to enter the bathroom right away, but my boyfriend had to wait for them to BREAK INTO THE BATHROOM with a putty knife....as a HUGE fight consisting of female McDonald's employees broke out in the street. It was insane. Screaming, clawing...we couldn't wait to get out of there (okay, who am i kidding, i ran out of the bathroom without drying my hands to see this spectacle..). 

FInally the employees were able to pry the men's bathroom door open and we were able to make a swift exit. 

Only in Philly?
Manager or Owner is always there making sure that the place is in tip top shape.  Great service and very clean.  This is by far the best McDonalds I have ever been to.

the service here was better than I've seen at any mcdonald's.  I had a chance to speak w/ the owners of the store also, and they were some of the nicest people I've ever met - super friendly and definitely cared about their customers!  Their dedication to customer service definitely showed in every single employee.
Updated with one extra star in recognition of their recent efforts to become ever-so-slightly less horrible.

So being a college student isn't  so great when it comes to having the time and money to go eat somewhere great. Especially through this bad economy where a dollar is so hard to spend and so hard to get, I needed something cheap and decent. After spending my morning studying, my brother and I decided to go for McDonald's. We ordered two 10 piece chicken nuggets and a Big Mac Meal. This is very unhealthy, and i recommend you all not to do this on the regular. I had my 10 piece nuggets and it was great! Crispy on the outside, soft and juicy in the inside. The service was great. I gave them the money, they gave me the correct change back which was quite impressive. Took less than 2 minutes to get my food and cup. They could work on cleaning the tables a bit more. I found a leftover french fry laying on my table which I flicked off the table. 


but seriously, I'm not a big fan of fast food and probably won't be back til next never.
Steer clear of this fast food outlet. Even for a McDonald's, the food here is quite sub par not to mention the poor service.

On top of this MCD, you will get the same owners at 38th and Illinois, 16th and Meridian, and 71st (?) and Keystone, and Emerson and I-465.  Again, the same experience with this franchisor everytime.  Bad service, not accepting of any coupons.  The Emerson location actually charged me MORE one time when I had a coupon for a free sandwich with the purchase of a drink, then if I had purchased the meal outright with no promo coupon (which was a hotel promo at the time in which people paid a special rate to recieve the promo.)

Pathetic, money-grubbing owners will produce pathetic, money-grubbing managers, who will produce pathetic, underpaid employees who hate their jobs.  Good job "Faith and Blessed McDonald's of Indianapolis" for being the stereotype of a poorly run, urban company.  For an example of how urban customer service can flourish, see Yats.

As far as fast food chains go, this is definitely in my top 10. I was hungry, and because it was a nice day, I decided to eat in my car. The drivethrough was very convenient for this purpose. Each time I wanted more food I just drove out to the highway and turned around at the next light, then on back into the parking lot for another round with the delightful and helpful staff. I ended up eating about 6 or 7 burgers, one at a time to let them hit my tummy (watching my weight, those khakis are getting tight).

My only complaint was the pickles - when I made a movement the next day they didn't exactly make for solid structure.

These people are slow.  The slowest McDonalds by far.  They cannot speak English well.  Every other time I'm there my order is wrong and I have to get it fixed.  I can't understand what they are saying most the time.  All of the workers speak mostly Spanish and very little English.  Everytime I go back and see a new employee I think "Oh great, maybe this one speaks English!" Sadly, I am let down because once again they do not understand me, I do not understand them and my order is all wrong.  Now let me state I'm not prejudice and I'm all about giving people a chance.  I do believe Americans need to learn more than 1 language in school and I think the borders should be "open" without discrimination, but I wish they would hire competent people at McDonald's that at least know the language enough to take an order. I have many other complaints dealing with their hiring practices, but for some reason Yelp took it down, so I guess I can't tell you. The food is also cold and the fries are over-salted and cold. I try to avoid this place like the plague.  I go 1 exit over for better service in Lemmon Valley.

This place is much improved from how it was before the new management took over about a year ago. That being said, if the souplines of the 1930s were to have a modern equivalent, they would be this McDonald's. I've personally been repeatedly panhandled in the store. Someone fired a gun in the store a few months ago. The speed of the service is slower than average. (Then again, it seems like pretty much every Philadelphia fast food establishment is a bit on the pokey side.) If you have some sort of coupon or discount, expect to wait a good six minutes for the cashier to find the manager. Waiting that long made me wish I hadn't asked for ten cents off.

I've got to say the worst thing that's happened here has been when I have ordered soft serve. These guys are perfectionists! They will pour me a cone, decide that it isn't perfectly shaped, open the top of the soft serve machine, dump the ice cream back into it, and then pour me the cone again! In addition to being a potential health code violation, this sure makes it take a long time for me to get my cone! (This has happened more than once.)

Went here out of desperation.  Pulled up to see a group of skateboarders and smelly homeless people.  Decided to leave my hungry bunch in the car as I ventured inside.  The place smells but is not a surprise because of the clientele that walk aimlessly about.  The service wasn't that bad despite the fact that there seemed to be only 3 people working and one of them was in the seating area sweeping the floors and the tables.  Yes I said tables.  If I knew the area better probably would've looked for someplace else.

This McDonalds was the first fast food restaurant in D-town and it is still there today.  As McDonald's go it is well run and fairly clean.  It is, however, a McDonald's after all and I just can't stand their food.  Maybe the fries are OK, but I am not a fast food lover.

This mcdonalds would get a one star it has slow serving time and the food is average but I give it 5 stars because of one exceptional employee Justin you have to say hi to him if you stop by here he makes the best food ever and he's mad cool and had lots of girls he's the celebrity of browns mills mcdonalds he should deffeniatley be the store manager
Just a Reg mcdonalds. Their drove through is always fast and for the most part friendly.

This is a great Mcdonalds if you want your order screwed up. I have been several times and everytime i order a burger and up with a salad. I think if you have to go use small words and sound them out so they understand

This McDonald's, for lack of a better word, SUCKS!!!

1) Wanted to charge me extra for a sweet and sour sauce since I was already given two barbecue sauces...so I did an exchange
2) Coffee was so old that it had that sour taste
3) French fries were old and not crispy...they literally tasted a couple of hours old
4) One of the bathroom sinks didn't work - no water would come out
5) No soap in the bathroom so I guess the employees don't wash their hands
6) One of the bathroom stalls didn't have toilet paper 

And this place is supposed to be a McCafe....I thought they were supposed to be better than a regular McDonalds. Other than having nice booths, this McDonalds sucks!!

OK, I'm gonna be nice and give them 2 stars - as usually McDonald's by it's very nature is a one star chain for me. 

I don't do fast food.  I just don't - but if you need a clean(ish) restroom - and the new McCafe coffee - the New Britain (old school) mcD's has been around for-eh-ver.

I think it may be about the same vintage as the Doylestown location.

The people working here are pleasant, though and that is worth alot.  Mostly CB West folks, some young adults - some not-so-young (during the day shift).

I won't be in often, but hey - it's there.

Decided to eat here because everything in downtown Kenner was closed! I had a salad which was good. The ladies working here were super warm and nice. The black coffee was very watery and I asked them if I can have another cup. The second one was still watery yet it wasn't as bad as the first.

Run by "Faith and Blessed." Well, their faith didn't bless them with the ability to hire non-crackheads who can get a fast food order right or do it in under 10 min. without tons of side conversations.  Constantly overstaffed and under preforming.   one time, they actually refused to give me my drink cuz "you won't hear you order."  Another time I had to wait 15-20 min for my order, at 5:30am! All the ones this company runs are this way, thankfully they put up signs everywhere so you know which ones to avoid.     Proof positive that the more you talk about Jesus, the less you have to act like him.

Damn, we really shut the city down that night...After a long night downtown, we returned to the Opryland area...Our hotel is here, is anything open?, Searching the Gaylord Opryland Resort, we were greeted at the lobby by a Mexican guy with a 12-pack of beer.  He was pretty generous, sharing his beer, however everything was closed...this didn't keep us out of the bar though (what a night, huh?).

Eventually, we realized the party was over, but I wanted to grab a bite to eat, so I said goodbye to my friends, jumped in a cab and had the driver take me to nearby McDonald's...

My Somalian driver, Mos asked me to lean over and order.  As I stared up at the menu and ordered my Big Mac combo (as pictured on the menu board), I was told that there was no way I could enjoy a burger today...not just because they are unenjoyable, but because the time is now 4:55 AM and they're switching over to breakfast...Damn you, I don't want your eggs!!

I had a hashbrown and a large Coke, and ordered a large Sprite for my cab driver (the nearby drive-thru liquor store was not open yet)...

While some people race to get to McDonald's before 10:30 so they can have breakfast, I now know I need to show up far before 5 AM to avoid it...

I used to have a silly mustache.  It was long and thin (extending about 4 inches or so into the air).  I had it for three years.  I used it as a prop for my pro wrestling habit.

One time, while in the area, I decided to stop into this McDonald's.  I waited in line until it was my turn to speak to the girl at the counter.

Perhaps she had never seen a mustache before.  It must have been something new for her, as she immediately began to laugh in my face over it.

Now, wearing a ridiculous stache like that, you have to take the reactions with a grain of salt.  I knew this.  It didn't bother me.  I was used to it.

Except, this girl started to laugh uncontrollably at me.  In fact, so much so that she wouldn't take my order.  Instead, she called over a large group of McDonald's workers to look at me... all the while pointing at me and wetting themselves with glee and cackling.  Much like at the circus.  Much like the pack of hyenas in The Lion King.

Even so, it wouldn't have been so horrible.  Except it wasn't a HA HA I'm with you on the joke.  It was malicious laughing.  Belittling laughing.

You can imagine all the ignorant, ghetto trash things they said to me.  Let's face it.  They WERE ghetto trash, and they worked in McDonald's in Philadelphia.  This isn't an indication of race or socioeconomic status -- just a statement on our town. 

Of all the travesties of manners and customer service I've endured in Philly fast food establishments, this experience was perhaps the most damning and indicative of the type of slugs that inhabit this city's minimum wage workforce.
I usually drive through here for breakfast between 7:30 and 8:00 AM and they are usually pretty spot on with the whole experience: food, friendliness, and speed.
Never had a bad experience at this location and the drive-thru is 24 hours which is great for those late night cravings :P

Service is extraordinarily polite from the cashier.  However, the food preparation needs dire work.  They've gipped us on the fries twice.  They don't seem to fill the fries to the brink of the container.

I drive home to my parents  fairly often and I find myself usually getting the munchies upon arrival into DE, which is about another 45 min - an hour from my parents.' I've stopped here a many occasion. Drive thru is nice and quick and going in to the counter hasn't delayed me too much, especially when the drive thru looks backed up. The food is pretty standard for McD (3 stars). +1 star for the service. Even when it was my fault for the misorder (as was the case last month), they fixed it for me and gave me what I meant to order, but didn't (it was the same price as what I ordered but didn't mean to)

By far the nicest McDonald's in the city (that I have been to).

Let's face it.  Eating fast food in this city is an experience that makes you either want to kill yourself, the worker serving it to you, or the other patrons in the restaurant.  But this particular location makes you forget about that (kind of)... and for that I give it a thumbs up (relative to Philadelphia fast food).

Why?

The ambiance is a step up from other cookie cutter incarnations in that it is in the lobby of an older, more statuesque building near City Hall.  The ceilings are high, and the floor to ceiling windows encompass the length of the seating area providing good light and good people watching.  The cleaning crew is usually on task in an effort to make the tables and spills cleaned, and the counter people are typically a cut above other locations.  Transient and homeless campers are kept to a minimum.  AND -- You get to pour your own soda, which is always a plus for me!

One potential negative is the cold draft that blows in from the Arch St. door when opened during the winter.  In the summer, however, the breeze is quite pleasant.  The Broad St. door is a rotating circle door, which is fun.

The food is the food... and a McDonald's is a McDonald's is a McDonald's... except, probably due to the location, this one is a bit better than the rest in Philly.

Part of me feels ridiculous reviewing a McDonald's: they all have the same "cuisine," and it's all pretty mediocre.  So the only thing to go by is the character of the restaurant, and the various features that differentiate one restaurant from another.

This one has a little more character, but that's not why it's so great.  Since it's very close to the Opryland Hotel, it feels the need to give us a theme with enclosed exhibits.  They're not country music, but more like Old Time Radio.  They are pretty cool, but they'll only hold your attention for a minute or so.  Another irony is the fact they sell crappy Nashville and Opry souvenirs: The usual crap, no point getting into it.

But the great part comes in how they treat customers and the features.  Knowledgeable fast food aficionados know that thousands of McDonald's restaurants installed wifi, and Nashville is no different.  But this McDonald's has a large screen television, as well as smaller TVs throughout the restaurant, and I have found that they have the sense to put on important programming on at the right times.

Combine these two, and you have an excellent experience at certain times.  The upcoming winter olympics is a prime example.

I went in at a down time, Sunday evening around five-thirty, and there was almost no traffic.  It was probably because of this, that they didn't object when I extended my power cord across the walkway.  It wasn't really a trip hazard, but they certainly could have made a scene about it.  As it was, I could comfortably watch the programming and tweet and follow my message board with ease.  There were some other people who brought in an extension cable and (I believe) a surge protector, and were involved in some heavy duty internet gaming.

I appreciate that this McDonald's let their customers go a little crazy.  I was geeking out and TVing, and the hardcore gamers were using a lot more bandwidth than I was.  So I'll call my creating obstacles and their bandwidth-suck a draw.  I admit, it would have been a jerk move on my part had there been a significant number of customers, but the place was pretty dead, and I am sure that's part of the reason, they let me hang for about an hour and a half (and who knows how long hardcore gamers were there: they even stopped for a smoke break).

Now it would take a near-miracle for Mickey D's to rate five stars, since the food is pretty crappy, but a four-star quality experience just cannot be ignored.   Thanks for making Super Sunday worth my while McDonald's.

OK, I was brought up on Mcky'D's. I must tell you, you're better off going to the Mullica Hill Restaurant. The one in Woodstown has fallen incredibly hard! I don't know where they're getting these employees from but I can tell you this, It's main business is supplying travelers with a bathroom either to or from the shore. As far as the service, POOR. And it has changed in the last 6 months. I watched as my pancake hit the ground with at least 6 laughing employees standing around joking around doing nothing. The girl put it in the container and I said I didn't want it. The manager saw this and the employee complained "I didn't drop it!". You can wait in the drive through sometimes for 5 mins. or more with no one in the store! The Salem N.J. McDonalds is the same way. I would avoid the fast foo and head to the local diners! Skip the sodium Burger!

Hey, this is part of my fast food reviews OK? Listen, It's MC DONALD'S, not Gourmet food. Service, Cleanliness, All Great. Hey, you'll even get your food hot! And the fries, Not a Package of Little ends! It has a play area for the little ones. The best McDonald's in this part of Gloucester and SALEM COUNTIES.
Perfect place to pick up a sausage burrito before hopping on your SEPTA or Amtrak train.  All aboard!

Staff were efficient, though not friendly or happy.
Fast Food - ok speed
Food better than the average McDonalds
Bathroom was horrible,  The urnial was broken,  The bathroom was filthy with grafitti on the walls.  Makes you wonder what the back of the kitchen looks like.

Of COURSE you shouldn't eat there every day. Is that news to anyone? It's an American classic, and the kids who work there have been consistently nice and efficient on my last five visits.  I go only once a week, I swear, but only if I've worked out.  Or planned to work out.  Or spoke to someone who once did a sit-up.  My favorite, like you care:  two cheeseburgers, large fries and a large vanilla shake.  And you have to eat it like you just don't care!  Served American style, parked in front of your TV.  It's my favorite reward meal.  It's what I each to cheer myself up.  And the warden already knows it's my last meal.    I am a fan of the drive-through (especially if there actually IS ever a warden in my life).  Inside is getting a bit worn.  I think my 18-year-old played in that kiddie gym when she was three.  Come on corporate McDonald's!  It's the Main Line!  That place should be sparkling!  But, seriously, some of the kids who work at the window must have paid attention in training.  And the food is as remarkably consistent as it's supposed to be.  Ok, I go on a diet tomorrow.  No, Friday.   Definitely Satur . . . . Sunday.  Monday I start watching what I eat . . . .

This McDonald's is golden. No pun intended. 

Seriously though, it is great. Food wise it is obviously the same as all other McDonald's restaurants. It is newer so it looks newer and more modern. The best part is it now comes with TV's. Honestly I never go into McDonald's to eat anymore, drive thru is the way to go. However, this one is open 24 hours and that's not just drive thru. You can go inside and sit down if you wish. So a late night meal here when everything else is closed down isn't bad at all and the TV's help keep you entertained. 

I think all the new McDonald's carry TV's now, as they should.

I realize this may be kind of a cop out, but It's hard to accurately judge an establishment you've only eaten at a handful of times. Not for lack of trying, mind you! They're just never open at night. That's right, this 24-hour McDonald's is NEVER OPENED between the hours of 12am and 6am. 

I work the graveyard shift and this McDonald's is one of only half a dozen establishments who are purportedly open at night. But anytime I go there, between the above listed hours, there is no one at the helm. The lights are on, there are people inside- presumably doing something to earn their graveyard shift differential pay- but no one answers the drive thru intercom. 

Their sign proudly announces that this McD's boasts a 24-hour drive thru, but there are no signs that lists their hours of operation. No signs that identifies their store number.

Out of frustration one time I drove up to the window and tapped on the glass. Luckily one of the workers had the courage to confront me and I asked as politely and calmly as I could, something to the effect of "is this a 24 hour drive thru or not?" 

To which the employee informed me simply, "not in a row."

As a McDonald's lover, I didn't think it was possible to dislike eating it until I went to the location on Girard... twice.

The first time I frequented this location it was 2pm on a Sunday and I've never before felt as uncomfortable in a restaurant. Between the obviously drugged out clientele and the unfriendly, half-asleep cashier, I wanted to leave this establishment as soon as possible and ended up eating my meal in my car.

The second time I went, I opted for the drivethru. While the service was better and smiles were exchanged, the food was not up to the McDonald's standards.  The soda was short on syrup and the burger/bun were both overcooked. Burgers are not easy to eat while driving, I will admit this, but the mayonnaise had missed the burger for the most part and was globbed on the outside of the box, ended up on my steering wheel, pants, and hands.

I agree with Jill though; the fries were good.

Where do I begin? The very first thing I noticed as I walked in the door was an obviously drunk man hanging out by the order counter. He reeked of alcohol and kept harassing the staff, poking fun at customers, and butting into conversations. I was absolutely amazed that McDonald's didn't see fit to throw him out. Secondary factors detracting from the admittedly mediocre experience were they don't give out cups for water and they limit the dipping sauces, charging extra if you need more than the amount allotted for your chicken nuggets. Also, they didn't give me the sauces I requested and I only found out about it after I got home and opened the takeout bag, but given all the above, that's a pretty minor problem.

"Not until I've had my morning coffee"

... This is where I get my morning caffine fix.  And they always seem to get it right. $1.49 for a large.

The McDonald's in Meadowood Mall is a rouge operation. They change from breakfast to lunch whenever they feel like it. Once they switch their menu board they become fast food Nazi's! 

"No breakfast for you, come back one year" 

Not that it will do any good, but here is the web address to complain... 

http://www.mcdonalds.com/contact/contact_us.html

I'm McHating it.

I wanted a chicken sandwich.  I waited twenty minutes and was told the wait was due to the staff not knowing how to make chicken sandwiches.  How does that even happen?  

My order was wrong, twice.  

This place is only for the serious masochist.

This is one McDonald's that I've seen quite a number of times but never went in until this afternoon. The food was about what you can expect for McDonald's. Service was a bit better than expected. And unlike some other McDonald's, they haven't started charging for water cups.

This mc donalds if fine most of the time.  The do have a tendancy to use stale oil for the fries and hash browns which makes them taste horrible.  And if you've gona through the drive through like I have especially during breakfast hours- I didn't realize that until I got too far away to return and complain.
Over the staff is accomodating, not very personable at all but what do you expect from young folks working fast food these days- not a lot.

Stopped in here on Saturday afternoon to score the seasonal cult favorite - the Shamrock Shake. Best Shamrock Shake I've ever tasted, and it was the perfect shade of Shamrock Shake green and made my sunny Saturday afternoon that much happier. 

This McDonald's was clean, bright, busy - and the Shake was served quickly and with a smile. Almost made me want to order a Big Mac and some fries too....but I restrained mysefl. But if I ever get a random craving for chicken mcnuggets, I know where to go...

McDonald's has had some good days and some bad (they are inconsistent). When I go through the drive- through, the service is usually good, but not great. Their french fries are good, but are very greasy. Same with their hamburgers. When you order a Big- Mac, it's not all up to what it seems. Yes, it's good, but it isn't that big. Some days I like their food, and others I don't. Like I said before, McDonalds is inconsistent.

Why is a newly stamped Yelp Elite (YAY!) writing a review of a McDonalds?  Well, it has nothing to do with the food.  In fact, I didn't even eat there, but I had to stop somewhere to use the bathroom after shopping at Downington Coins and Stamps, so I went here, which is at the intersection of Rte 100 and Swedesford Road.  

I've never seen a McDonalds quite like it.  The first thing I noticed was the walnut-like finish all over, then the decorative waterfall thingy in the very clean dining area, which had tables and seats and cozy booths that were much more upscale than expected.  The bathroom was pretty nice, and the kids play area was the clincher. It was entirely enclosed along with an extra seating area, and featured not only those tube things, but an air hockey table as well.  Basically, this place was the most upscale McD's I've ever seen, and considering that they don't have to bother, I walked away impressed.  Maybe I'll try the food someday, who knows.
I've been to McDonald's Restaurants in most states. This is the best McDonald's ever. Ever.

Let's face it, it's McDonald's - Who doesn't love the greasy goodness of those crisp, salty fries? This visit, I tried the Shamrock Shake. What is this green monster? It's not quite minty, it was a bit fruity, it wasn't great but it wasn't terrible. So my curiosity is still peaked.
I stop here every morning and the coffee is always great and the girls are always friendly. They even remember how I want it and don't need to ask so it makes things go a little faster for me.
This is one of my least favorite McDonald's and we only stop there if we have to.  Our order is incorrect a lot of times, and the fries are always WAY too salty and even my toddler will not eat them.

This place has the CHEAPEST 20 piece Chicken McNuggets for $4.99!

I know, I couldn't believe it either but it's true, I saw it with my own twos! This McD's is also the only place that I've been to that sells a chocolate dipped vanilla cone for $1.19.

Need I say more?

Yes, it's McDonald's and before people started criticizing we ALL were chowing down those delicious Big Macs and yummy french fries. They're trying to make dues so don't dislike them for that.

Anyways, cheapest McNuggets and chocolate dipped vanilla cones - what else could you want?

I'll be sure to come back, oh yes, I do!

Four thumbs up since the person who ate my McFlurry agrees!

nothing can satisfy my tummy after some drunken debauchery at Smoke's like mickey D's on 40th and walnut.  the characters you meet there make your experience all the better.  I WILL MISS YOU MCDONALDS.

-Penn Senior
I stopped at this McDonald's only because I happened to be passing through this area. I don't expect much from McDonald's but this place was clean and service was good enough.

took about 25 minutes for all of us to get our food.  some of us got sick after eating here not sure why...the place was a mess and it was dirty. the tables needed to be wipe down.  we only came here since it was the only thing open at 10pm on a friday night.

Ahhhh, my old stomping grounds. I couldn't tell you how many times I've been to this McDonald's. Probably because I don't remember half of them.

The big draw to this McDonald's is its location - right in the 30th st station. Most of their customers are travelers grabbing food at the train station. Back when I used to take the R8 to work every day, I was indeed one of them - although for breakfast, I preferred the Dunkin Donuts across the aisle.

However, this location served another purpose - drunk Drexel students. At least when I went to school there, you had one location on campus open 24 hours to get food - 7-11. As delicious as those taquitos are, sometimes you need something else. That's what the 24 hour McDonald's in 30th st station is for.

The problem? Its only 24 hours in spirit. Many, many times, if you come between the hours of 2-5, the employees will just be lounging around. They're "closed to get ready for breakfast" they'll say. In other words, they want to get paid to sit around and do nothing, while poor me goes hungry. Oh, and their prices are higher than the standard McDonald's, too. And its not always clean.

The location advantage saves this McD from a 1-star. If you're at 30th st station during the day, you have many other options available to you. Use them.

Only one reason to review a McDonald's in my book: This one sold Shamrock Shakes in 2010, up through St. Patrick's Day. 

It was the strangest presentation of it I've ever seen, though. They served it in their "McCafe" coffee cups, put whipped cream & a cherry on top. Never in my glorious 30 years of consciousness about Shamrock Shakes had I gotten whipped cream or a cherry. Kinda small, kinda pricey, definitely did not care, because in 2009, I drove all the way to Ohio for one for the wife.

For that, Clown Boy, you get three stars. Otherwise?

This is the worst Mickey D's  have ever been to.  I am usually a fan of Mc Donald but this one always has trouble getting the order right.  And the last time the food was terrible.  The fish for the fish sandwich tasted like it was refried after sitting for hours, along with the Bic Mac we got.  Totally disappointed!

Don't already have enough reason to stay away from soulless corporate chains while you're in a culinary capital? Yesterdays events should be more than enough to scare off even the most gluttonous tourist from their McFatty Patty. Marring an otherwise OUTSTANDING French Quarter Fest a couple of delinquent thugs decided to settle scores with guns right in front of this McDonals.  Seven people were shot.  I've seen many teens hanging out here during late night hours. McDonalds should really have a security guard posted 24-7 at this location.  

This event was not quite as bad as the murders at Louisiana Pizza Kitchen many years ago (nobody dies in this battle per news reports), but so disappointing and unnerving to say the least.  Oh, and our cops marked the shell casings with Tropical Isle cups.  I'm not quite sure what to make of that.

This smaller McDonalds is updated and new.  The lot is small, so drive-through can wrap around the building.  But go inside.  It's usually empty.  Wi-Fi is good, they have a flat screen TV on the wall, and it's always clean.

Oh... and there's no kids play area which is a plus for me since I don't have any children.

I have been going through this McDonald's every workday morning between 7:00-7:45AM for about 4 months now.

They consistently get my breakfast order correct, they always include the napkins, flatware, condiments etc. & there's that sweet Jamaican lady at the first window who always acknowledges you with her accented "Good mornin' dear!"

I'm not sure how this place works during other times of the day, but during breakfast time, it cranks out food like a well-oiled machine.

The only reason this place gets one star is that it is the lowest I can rate it... so I give this star to the sweet girl who tried to take my order.  This place deserves ZERO stars because of this... my husband and I walk in 5 minutes before they stop serving breakfast... as I step up to the register I ask if they are still serving breakfast and the kind girl at the counter says "yes we are" and then we see that in five minutes they will be serving lunch which my husband wants so he will order later and I will order now.  As I talk to the sweet girl about if I can get a breakfast burrito with only egg a manager says "they are pre-made and I cannot," so as I look to order another breakfast item the rude manager slides the menu to lunch and says, "we are no longer serving breakfast."  I stand amazed as they refuse to serve me breakfast even though it was probably actually at the time three minutes before they stop serving breakfast and decide that if they are going to be that rude they do not deserve my money nor the money of any ears I can reach.  Each time I come to Reno I will not step foot into this place unless I hear that something has been done to change the situation.
Get your breakfast here if you like your food burned.  Five times in a row and these idiots don't realize they're burning food.

It's a McDonalds - you get pretty much the same food every time so I'll give them kudos for food consistancy. However....

The two in Edwardsville are some of the most poorly run of any I've visted. Place is usually trashed, staff is indifferent and never in a hurry. They only take one register order at a time to fool corporate into thinking there are not long waits (timer starts when order is paid for at register.). Speaking of corporate - doesn't anyone ever check these places? This is Edwardsville and I think that is the only thing saving them - so many people with money to spend that they end up getting "some" customers everyday.

check your bag before pulling off!

I often stop at the drive thru leaving z-hills to head back to Tampa and almost every visit, something was missing. Once it was my free coke glass, once they gave me a medium fry instead of a large and this last visit they didnt give my friend any sweet and sour sauce for her nuggets. 

The good thing about this McDonalds is the food is consistantly hot and fresh. The fries have always been crisp and perfectly salted and the coke I swear is as cold as Poland in the winter lol.

The time is 9:00 pm. A young Indian male named Jeff walks up to the door and pulls only to find it locked. Inside, he notices two McDonald's employees (one of them the manager) flirting with two very unattractive women whose only redeeming qualities are that one could use her backside as a shelf. The two women are let out by the manager. Jeff is visibly disturbed at how they (the women) keep looking at the man in what one can only assume are meant to be looks of seduction while they eat their ice cream sloppily. Jeff looks at the hours of operation sign which states that they are open until 10:00 pm.

[Jeff]: Are you closed? :\
[Manager]: Yeah.
[Jeff]: The sign says 10.
[Manager]: We're closing because no one wants McDonald's right now.
[Jeff]: I'm. right. here. (actually raises hand)
[Manager]: ... (locks door and walks off)
[Jeff]: ... (stands there in stunned silence)
[Unattractive woman]: (giggles)

Jeff finds this kind of funny (after).

I like this McDonald's!  It's probably 4.5 stars, for a McD's, but I feel guilty cluttering up the St. Louis area recommendations with such a relative recommendation.

This place is very clean, very comfortable, and there's lots of parking to be had, too.  Everything's in place to fix that fast food craving or offer a quick coffee via drive-through.

(Andrew M. gives the place a hard time for not really being 24-hour.  I've never tried coming at off hours, so I can't say much to that.)

If you're looking for fast food, maybe driving through the area or something, you won't go wrong here.

Been here for drive-through a few times. It's fine; they got my order correct and they kept the line of vehicles moving steadily. 

Solid!

This is a newer McDonalds in an up an coming little area of Hwy 100...I have stopped in here several times for a quick bite or something sweet while in the area and the service has always been quick and friendly, food is freshly cooked, and the place is clean.  I must say this store stands out above several of the others in the local area not just because it is new (several of the others are too) but the staff!

I have tried this McDonalds three seperate times now...sorry to say it will be awhile before I give it a go again if I ever do.  The first two times the service has been only so so, but less than friendly.  The last time, on a Saturday, not even sure they had anyone working...people standing and waiting in the lobby with no one around.  No cars in the drive-thru either....two employees outside (one who was clearly off work or looked to be and one who seemed dressed for work and then walked in went to the back and was never seen again).  I left after waiting about five minutes as the people in front of us were still waiting.  The store was clean the first time I was in but that was when it was brand new, now not so sure but it wasn't filthy either and I understand what a saturday at a place can be like.  Food has been ok, had better and had worse as far as McDonald's goes....their service is their downfall.  Too bad as it is in a great location and they seem to have plenty of business.
My order was right and my son didn't yell at me!  Is there anything better than 2 MCD hamburgers when you are really hungry?  OOOps, yes there is McRibs!!!  I want my McRibs!!!

This McDonald's has been renovated on the inside since I was first there many moons ago. It's now faux fancy - for a McDonald's) - with trendyish light fixtures and an off-coffee color scheme.

The parking lot is still a weird two-level split.

Besides the face lift, this McDonald's is as good as any other in the region.
Crappy Service.  Management does nothing and collects a paycheck.  They have no idea what to do with the poisoned Shrek glasses or how to give me my money back.

If any place would benefit from business process redesign, it would be here, the 30th St. McDonalds in Philadelphia. 

I've never SEEN so many employees collectively involved in the mess-up of virtually every single order made. It's painful to watch, and even more painful to experience, especially when they decide it's you, and not they, who botched your order. 

One time an employee brimmed with rage because I failed to recognize that the soda she filled for me was mine. The one that was left to swelter by the deep frier, and probably had a straw in it. In fact she was so hot with anger, she nearly lept her poly-panted self right over the counter for what could very well have been a rigorous hair-pulling sesame-seed face-off.

And another thing. This location has no ketchup dispensers. Totally annoying!! When you need to eat fast and catch a train, you need to pump it. But instead, 30th St. only does ketchup packets: those tiny, impossible-to-open packets -- and only if you ask. Otherwise you get none.

1 out of 10 hamburger patties.

The service here is pretty slow at times but it is generally friendly.  There is plenty of parking but it gets very crowded after 9:30 and 11:30 Masses at MDP.  Lunch can also get busy and you might have to wait a little, even at the drive-thru.  The restaurant itself is pretty clean, and the fries are hot and crispy.  If you need a McDonald's fix and are in KoP, then this is it.

If I reviewed this McDonald's on the restroom alone, it would get 1 star. Nothing works in there. The urinal didn't flush. The cold water taps on both sinks were broken. Good thing the hot water wasn't that hot. The knob on the hot air dryer was loose and hanging down by a spring.

On the plus side, the dining room area seemed clean and ordering food was a no-fuss experience. Can't say that the food is superb but they made the sandwiches I ordered nicely enough.
Look around there isn't a place in Carperteria, Santa Barbara, or the general vacinity with a drive thru...they are not allowed by law in this area
This is virtually like any other McDonalds in Philly. It would be nice if they updated the decor and donated more of their moneys to charity.

Last time I was here I was hungover after a night of massive winning at the casino. Got the Big Breakfast and got a big stomach ache. 

To the wise, if you think you're still hungry, wait 20 minutes! Do not get more food.

It would never have occurred to me to rate a chain restaurant, maybe most especially McD but about twice a year I go in to satisfy some crazy primal urge. Yesterday was one of those visits. I don't want to comment on the food except to say it is what it is (I did notice that the Big Mac has gotten quite a bit smaller-probably a good thing, really) but what I did notice was that my fingers got sticky when I depressed the ketchup dispenser. When I looked I saw that this dispenser had probably not been cleaned since God Only Knows. I immediately  spoke to the person who appeared to be the manager (I should have checked, really) who offered a packet of ketchup instead and said, "I'll have someone take care of it right away." Yeah! While I indulged in those meaningless calories, I watched while nobody came to tend to it.
I was really annoyed so I wrapped a piece of napkin around the handle-it stuck all by itself-to see if anyone would notice. Nobody noticed so I finally asked for the manager and the lovely young lady I spoke with (not the manager) asked if SHE could help-imagine!!! She blocked the dispenser off and , sure enough, came back with cleaning equipment and began the job herself just as I was leaving. THAT should have been the manager's job-just take care of it now. Brava to you young lady-you should be the manager.
So, food, well okay, but cleanliness uh uh.

So I came here one night before the drive home from USF and was really hungry so I stopped at this McDonald's and ordered some food. The order went through and when I got to the window they had my food ready they passed it to me and then I handed them my debit card and they THEN told me that it was cash only...with the food already in my hands, I could already smell my meal and was ready to eat it. The lady asked for the food back and I handed it back to her pissed and still hungry. While I was in line before I saw someone angrily speed off and I imagine it was for the same reason.
Jane is spot on about this place. If you speak English head up the road to the other McDonald's. I have ate here a few times and every time the experience gets worse. Worst McDonald's in Reno by far.

This is the best McDonald's in the North America if not the world.

The other people who have reviewed this Mickey D's and said otherwise, well...I hate to tell you, but they have had their brains ruined by heroin and LSD.  Either that, or they are  involved in the evil Yelp extortion business model.
